entries.name: Broken Access Control
entries.description: Restrictions on what authenticated users are allowed to do are not properly enforced. Attackers can exploit these flaws to access unauthorized functionality and/or data.

entries.name: Cryptographic Failures
entries.description: Failures related to cryptography that often lead to sensitive data exposure or system compromise.

entries.name: Injection
entries.description: Untrusted data is sent to an interpreter as part of a command or query. Includes SQL, NoSQL, OS, LDAP, XPath, expression-language, and template injections.

entries.name: Insecure Design
entries.description: Risks related to design flaws — missing or ineffective control design that no implementation can save.

entries.name: Security Misconfiguration
entries.description: Improperly configured permissions, unnecessary features enabled, default accounts/passwords, missing security headers.

entries.name: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
entries.description: Using components with known vulnerabilities (libraries, frameworks, OS-level packages).

entries.name: Identification and Authentication Failures
entries.description: Weaknesses in confirming the user's identity, authentication, and session management.

entries.name: Software and Data Integrity Failures
entries.description: Software updates, critical data, and CI/CD pipelines without verifying integrity. Includes deserialization issues.

entries.name: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
entries.description: Insufficient logging, monitoring, or active response to detect and respond to breaches.

entries.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
entries.description: Attacker can induce the server-side application to make HTTP requests to an unintended location.
